messages:
Anna: quick sync — I'm proposing a compact "handoff signal" between edge/proxy and origin to avoid split-brain and give origins a deterministic fallback order. TL;DR: two lightweight options, plus rollout notes. pinging @Matt @Sudha for architecture take.

Matt: ok, high level sounds good. what's the exact surface? headers? grpc metadata? a small proto would help. also how do we avoid races when two regions try to become primary for same tenant?

Anna: thinking HTTP headers for hosted + gRPC metadata for private, so it stays transport-agnostic. minimal example: 
```
X-Residency-Intent: takeover
X-Residency-Token: rzn-abc123
X-Residency-Seq: 42
X-Residency-Allowed-Fallbacks: region,europe,any
```
Intent is one of {observe, takeover, handoff, release}. Token is opaque lease id. Seq increments on each intent change (monotonic).

Sudha: I like the token+seq because it's idempotent and easy to reason about. Two quick concerns: 1) who mints token and TTL semantics? 2) what happens on network partition where both sides see stale tokens?

Anna: good Qs. Proposal: control-plane mints tokens on a successful lease grant. TTL encoded in token metadata (short, e.g., 30s–2m) and origin always verifies token against local lease cache. On conflict origin should compare seq then token creation time. If both tokens appear concurrent, origin falls back to policy (prefer resident region or higher SLO tier).

Kevin: legal/regulatory angle: any signal must be considered defense-in-depth; we can't rely solely on headers for compliance. If intent == takeover but tenant has residency constraint, origin must still enforce residency check server-side (not only proxy). Also how should we represent "deny due to policy" to the caller? 451 or 403?

Sudha: agreed. Recommend: origin returns 409 (conflict) when handoff in progress and 451 when request would violate data residency laws. That way client vs operator can distinguish. We should document the exact semantics.

Matt: operationally, needing control-plane minted tokens means control-plane must be highly-available in all regions or we accept some added latency for cross-region mint. Can we allow a delegated signer (short-lived crypto sig) so edge can mint when control-plane unavailable?

Anna: yes — we discussed delegated JWT-like signed tokens. Option B: edge signs a small JWT with region, ttl, seq, and a key-id. Origin validates signature using rotated keys from control-plane. Tradeoff: faster local decisions but more key management complexity.

Sam: rollout question: how do we handle older proxies that don't send these headers? We need backward compatibility: if headers missing, origin should behave current-default (best-effort fallback) and emit a telemetry tag for later analysis. Also gradual opt-in per-tenant via config key seems safest.

Anna: agreed. Plan: 1) implement origin-side acceptance for headers (non-breaking) + telemetry; 2) opt-in flag per tenant in residency config; 3) optional delegated signing (opt-in infra mode) for Dedicated/Private; 4) canary in single region, then multi-region canary.

Kevin: telemetry items we need: counts of conflicting tokens, conflicts resolved by seq vs timestamp, 451 occurrences, per-tenant fallback chosen. Add tracing span annotation for the token values (hashed) so we can correlate without leaking PII.

Sudha: another nit — KV cache ownership: when origin sees takeover intent, it should not evict immediately. Suggest states: RECEIVED_INTENT -> PROBING (check local cache/locks) -> COMMIT/REJECT. During PROBING keep serving reads from cache and stall writes briefly until final decision. That reduces client-facing flakiness.

Matt: sounds reasonable. Need to specify max PROBING window (e.g., 250ms) and a hard deadline after which origin either commits or rejects to avoid long delays. Also consider backpressure propagation so clients get consistent errors.

Anna: proposed deadlines: probe_timeout=250ms, token_ttl=90s, max_retries_for_handoff=3. We'll surface these as defaults but allow per-tenant overrides.

infra-bot: deploy checklist created: rzn/handoff-signal-v1 -> create feature flag, add telemetry, add origin header parsing lib, add signed-token verification lib.

Sam: testing matrix: unit tests for header parsing + seq logic, chaos tests with split-brain, canary with 5 tenants, legal-case simulation returning 451. I'll own test plan.

Kevin: one more thing — make sure Private deployments with on-prem control-plane can rotate keys offline. Document key rollover procedure and emergency revoke flow.

Anna: thanks all. action items: Matt to write token validation spec (due EOD), Sudha to sketch origin state machine (tomorrow), Sam writes test plan (end of week), Kevin drafts compliance note for docs (end of week). I'll draft RFC follow-up with diagrams and sample headers. :thumbsup:

Matt: ack

Sudha: ack

Kevin: ack

Sam: ack

Anna: leaving this thread open for async comments, will post the first draft RFC link when ready.
